capabilities: register custom file extensions as editable in the vault
force-open files and render them as code with syntax highlighting
assign views to specific file types
create and rename files through modals
extras: Full documentation lives in a separate wiki the README links to; the project also has a custom brandbook and media license. Default setup only edits .TXT files; other extensions require manual configuration in settings.
intentEvidence: Obsidian does not, for some reason, have the ability to edit any file extensions that the user would like to edit
motivation: The author found existing plugins inconvenient for end users and wanted a simple but advanced way to open and register any extension.
problem: Obsidian cannot edit the file extensions a user chooses, and existing plugins that handle non-markdown files present them in awkward formats such as JSON on one line.

relations.evidence: render them as code just like in other code editing software (like Visual Studio Code

summary: Registers arbitrary file extensions in a vault so they can be opened, edited, and rendered as code views with syntax highlighting.
